Challenge: benchmark:sql-injection-golden
Current phase: INTAKE
Confirmed target stack: flask, mysql, python
Candidate vulnerability categories: SQLI
Relevant techniques: SQL injection, boolean oracle
Description: SQL_INJECTION benchmark case for sql-injection-golden.

payload.goal: Exploit the confirmed 3-column UNION injection in the department parameter of POST /api/warranty/check to directly dump challenge_settings.verification_token. First determine which of the 3 result columns is reflected in the HTTP response (matched flag / message body), then place the token-selecting subquery in that column and read the actual token value.
payload.rationale: Facts #4/#5/#6 already established a 3-column UNION SELECT works and a row exists, so the shortest path to the goal is a direct UNION SELECT of challenge_settings.verification_token rather than char-by-char extraction. Need to identify the reflected column first.

payload.goal: If UNION output is not visibly reflected, extract challenge_settings.verification_token character-by-character using boolean-blind SQLi in department, relying on the 'matched' boolean / message as the oracle. Use SUBSTRING(verification_token,i,1) comparisons against a candidate set, sending each predicate and its negation in identical request shapes and repeating to confirm stability, then assemble the full token.
payload.rationale: The true/false test in #3 and the boolean 'matched' signal in #2 give a reliable boolean oracle independent of UNION reflection, so a boolean-blind extraction is a viable parallel path to the exact token.

payload.goal: Extract challenge_settings.verification_token via MySQL error-based injection (e.g. EXTRAVALUE/UPDATEXML or a deliberate type/column error) placed in the department concatenation, capturing the DB error text that leaks the token or a substring of it. Confirm the error text differs between a benign value and the error payload.
payload.rationale: The response message reflects query/error content (#2), so MySQL 8 error-based extraction is a distinct channel that could dump the token in one shot without needing reflection of result rows.

payload.goal: Prove the department-parameter oracle semantics before running any long extraction: send explicit true- and false-predicate controls three times each (e.g. ' OR 1=1-- - vs ' OR 1=2-- -), plus a row-existence control and an empty/NULL-token control, and record whether `matched` tracks predicate truth or merely row existence, then read SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(verification_token) and LENGTH(verification_token) from challenge_settings so the extraction targets the right row and knows the exact token length.
payload.rationale: #19/#21 show matched:true for injected predicates, but #22/#23 crashed and their conclusions are unusable, so neither open extraction intent has a validated, stable true/false oracle or a proven row/length target. Establishing that (and row count/NULL state) is the cheap gate that makes the char-by-char work correct instead of guessing.

payload.goal: Calibrate a time-based blind channel as an independent fallback: inject BENCHMARK(<N>,MD5(1)) (and, if unfiltered, SLEEP) into the department concatenation, measure wall-clock time for a control request vs the delayed request over at least three repeats each, and report the reproducible delta. Do not attempt full extraction in this intent, only channel calibration.
payload.rationale: UNION reflection is dead (#18) and the boolean channel still needs validation (I1); a measured timing channel is a genuinely different observable that survives response-content quirks, and the retrieved prior explicitly notes BENCHMARK() as the MySQL sleep substitute if SLEEP is filtered.

payload.goal: Run one bounded, resumable extraction script against the boolean oracle: first binary-search LENGTH(verification_token), then binary-search each character with ASCII(SUBSTR(...))>mid using ' OR (...) -- - in department, persisting progress and printing the recovered token plus the exact number of HTTP requests used.
payload.rationale: #21 confirms injected predicates flip matched to true and the column exists, so boolean binary search is the direct path to the token; this restates the open boolean intent with a concrete binary-search/resumable implementation and a request budget. Gated on I1's oracle proof so it does not burn the budget on a misread signal.
